questions.subject: MATH
questions.stem: For a homework assignment, in a structured way, work through this problem: A tree has 4 vertices. How many edges does it have?

options.misconception: it wrongly allows one cycle
it adds two extra edges
it confuses edges with the degree sum

questions.explanation: Every tree on 4 vertices has exactly 4 minus 1 edges, which is 3, a defining property equivalent to being connected and acyclic. Choice B is a distractor: it wrongly allows one cycle. Choice C is a distractor: it adds two extra edges. Choice D is a distractor: it confuses edges with the degree sum.
questions.hint: A tree on v vertices always has v minus one edges.

questions.stem: In a problem-solving session, in a structured way, work through this problem: A full binary tree has 10 leaves. How many internal nodes does it have?

options.misconception: it assumes equal numbers of leaves and internal nodes

questions.stem: On a practice test, in a structured way, examine this scenario: How many spanning trees does the complete graph K_3 have?

options.misconception: it uses the wrong exponent in Cayley's formula
it bases the power on n minus one
it counts all labelings rather than trees

questions.explanation: By Cayley's formula the number of spanning trees of K_3 is n to the power (3 minus 2), which equals 3. Choice B is a distractor: it uses the wrong exponent in Cayley's formula. Choice C is a distractor: it bases the power on n minus one. Choice D is a distractor: it counts all labelings rather than trees.
questions.hint: Apply Cayley's formula n to the power n minus two.
